findings.text: item (2) says "On that door a second launcher racing on the first attempt is not refused", but a solo `crew shadow` launch mints a fresh run id inside `dispatch` (dispatch.py:1590, `run_id: str | None = None` passed by neither `shadow()` at dispatch.py:1144 nor its callers) and publishes neither a claim nor a pointer, because claim publication is skipped for shadow lineage (dispatch.py:2577) and the shadow's pointer is written only at the end of its own dispatch; so no resume, admission relaunch or second shadow can name that run id inside the marker window, and the refused-race defect has no reachable caller

findings.reason: the plan names a safe-sounding repair for the very failure mode it must not reintroduce, and the node needs to be told what protects that window instead of the released reservation (the live-worker refusal or a recorded supervisor on a rewritten hold).
findings.text: item (3) requires that a supervisor record which fails to write "releases the reservation it was meant to carry and fails the launch visibly", but the write happens after the supervisor has been spawned (dispatch.py:3533–3536), so the release and the visible failure both land while the worker runs: the hold that would refuse a second door is gone and the dispatch reports failure, which is the invitation to relaunch over a live worker this plan exists to prevent

findings.reason: one sentence naming the rename keeps the tree from carrying a test whose name states the opposite of the mechanism it exercises.
